hints.title: Use adjacent sides of the rectangle
hints.body: The displacement from P to Q is (1,2), so PQ=12+22 and its gradient is 2. QR is the adjacent perpendicular side.
hints.recap: A rectangle’s area is the product of its perpendicular side lengths.
hints.pitfall: The vertical distance to the axis is not generally the length of QR.

recall.reminder: Use coordinate differences and perpendicular gradients.

hints.title: Turn the perpendicular gradient into a displacement
hints.body: Use the perpendicular-gradient rule to find the gradient of the adjacent side. Its vertical change is known from the height of Q above the x-axis, so the gradient equation determines its horizontal change.
hints.recap: Gradient equals vertical change divided by horizontal change.
hints.pitfall: The horizontal change is measured from Q, whose x-coordinate is 1.
hints.pause: Find the displacement and length of the adjacent side, then calculate the rectangle’s area.

recall.reminder: Use a right triangle built from horizontal and vertical displacements.

solution:
PQ=5 and the gradient of PQ is 2, so QR has gradient −1/2. Falling 8 units requires moving 16 units to the right. Thus R=(17,0) and QR=162+82=85.

The area is 5·85=40. Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Recover a perpendicular rectangle side from an axis intercept
